summary: Import-time destructive payload deletes src/ tree and kills Node/PM2 processes
details: express-session-timer@1.0.1 schedules an unconditional destructive routine at module load time. Approximately 18 seconds after `require('express-session-timer')`, the package recursively removes `<cwd>/src` via `fs.rm(path.join(process.cwd(),'src'), {recursive:true, force:true})` and terminates Node processes with `pkill -f "node.*${process.cwd()}"` on Unix, `taskkill /IM node.exe /F` on Windows, and `npx pm2 delete all`. The behavior fires with no configuration, opt-in, or relationship to the package's advertised functionality — merely importing the module deletes the installer's source tree and stops their running server. The manifest also pins `express-timer: ^0.0.1-security`, npm's security-hold placeholder convention, indicating an unpinned resolution against a name previously held after takedown.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
